items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I wrote a fellow up in Toledo had a band called Frank Terry's Chicago Nightengales... I went up there as his musical director and arranger and saxophone player.

ctx.x: Yeah. So at the intermission I was going out, get a little air, you know, have a little taste. So Frank Terry says to me, wait a minute, I want you to hear something? I said, what do you want me to hear? He says, I want you to hear a piano player. I said, man, I don't want to hear no piano player, I've heard all the greats, I heard Earl Hines when I was in Chicago, and Casno Simpson (phonetic) he played in Bernie Young's band, Casno Simpson, we had two pinaos. We had Burdett's Loving Good and Casno Simpson on…

So as I was just about to go out the door I heard this crescendo on the piano. They brought this kid up on the bandstand, led him up on the bandstand and I heard this great crescendo on the piano and I turned around and went back. And it was Art Tatum. And he started out playing Tiger Rag, right
